meta.title: Unified Funnel Platform - Scope, Architecture and Replacement Plan
meta.status: Draft for client discussion. Nothing in this document is built yet.
meta.audience: Business owners and decision makers first; engineers second. Plain wording is used on purpose.
how_to_read: Section 'summary' gives the whole idea in a few lines.
Section 'current_state' describes what exists today, taken from the actual funnel code.
Sections 'platform_structure' and 'roles_and_access' describe how the product is organised and who sees what.
Section 'modules' lists everything we propose to build, one module at a time.
Sections 'what_we_replace' and 'what_we_do_not_replace' are the honest boundary of the project.
Sections 'flows' and 'architecture' explain how it runs.
Sections 'phases', 'dependencies_and_running_costs', 'risks' and 'open_questions' are for planning and sign-off.
assumptions_flagged: Razorpay stays as the single payment gateway. It was named as the payment integration in the brief. If the intent is to remove Razorpay as well, see open_questions Q1.
How a landing page connects to the central platform is decided by the client. This document proposes a default and keeps the connector replaceable. See modules.landing_page_connector.
All tracking, workflow, lead storage and reporting are built in-house and run on the client's own infrastructure.

summary.one_line: One self-owned platform where every landing page, every payment, every lead and every follow-up lives, replacing a stack of paid third-party tools and Excel sheets.
problem_today: Each brand or landing page is built and run with a different mix of tools: a workflow tool (Pabbly), a tracking tool (Trackify-style), spreadsheets, and separate dashboards.
Every tool is a separate subscription, and every client pays for them separately, month after month.
Lead and payment data ends up in Excel. Sales teams work from spreadsheets, so there is no single source of truth, no access control and no audit trail.
Nobody can see in one place which landing page, ad or campaign actually produced revenue.
Automations (success message, failure message, follow-up) live inside a third-party tool that the client does not own and cannot easily inspect.
proposed_solution: A central platform with a Super Admin on top, brands under it, and many landing pages under each brand.
Each landing page connects to the platform using a defined connection method and its own configuration (offer, price, payment keys, workflow, tracking).
Every visit, lead, payment attempt, payment result and follow-up is stored in the platform's own database and shown on dashboards.
Role-based access: Super Admin, Management, Manager, Sales and Developer each see only what their role allows, enforced on the server.
An in-house workflow engine replaces Pabbly. An in-house first-party tracking system replaces Trackify-style tools. Excel is replaced by dashboards plus on-demand export.
Razorpay (payments), the WhatsApp Business API, and the ad platforms (Meta, Google) remain external because they cannot be self-hosted. They are integrated directly, with no middle tool.
expected_outcomes: One login and one dashboard for sales, managers, management and developers.
No monthly subscriptions for workflow or tracking tools.
Complete lead and payment history per landing page, including failed payments and abandoned checkouts.
Revenue attributed to campaigns and ads.
Configuration of a new landing page without developer involvement once the connector is in place.
Data owned by the client, on the client's infrastructure.
what_this_is_not: It is not a replacement for Razorpay, WhatsApp, Meta Ads or Google Ads themselves.
It is not a general website builder like Wix or Webflow in phase 1. Landing pages are still built as code and then connected.
It is not free to run. Hosting, payment gateway fees and WhatsApp conversation charges continue. Only the tool subscriptions go away.

current_state.source: Read from the 'funnel' project folder on 2026-10-17.

project.name: FUME Funnel (FUME.Fit)
project.framework: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4
project.purpose: Mobile-first VSL landing page for paid traffic from Meta (Facebook and Instagram) selling a 1:1 Root-Cause Consultation.

offer.refund_policy: Refund if the session is not useful

project.deployment: Serverless friendly (Vercel recommended). Home page is lp-2.
git_history_signals: Home page switched to lp-2; old base site dropped.
Razorpay checkout and Pabbly webhooks added.
Checkout hardened: phone normalisation, field length caps, noindex, fake live-viewer count removed.

routes.description: Landing page lp-2 (hero video, offer, bonuses, value stack, guarantee, testimonials, founder, decision, final CTA).
Alternative landing page variant lp-1 with its own styles and sections.
Checkout form (name, email, phone) that opens Razorpay.
Creates a Razorpay order (amount in rupees converted to paise) with customer details stored in order notes.
Verifies the Razorpay signature (HMAC SHA-256) and then notifies Pabbly of success.
Called when Razorpay reports payment.failed; reads customer details back from the order notes and notifies Pabbly of failure.

payment_flow_today: Visitor fills name, email and phone on /checkout.
The page calls /api/razorpay/order. The server creates a Razorpay order and returns order id and key id.
Razorpay Checkout opens in the browser.
On success the browser posts the three Razorpay values to /api/razorpay/verify. The server checks the signature, fetches the order, and posts a success payload to a Pabbly Connect webhook.
On failure the browser posts to /api/razorpay/failed. The server posts a failure payload to a second Pabbly webhook.
Everything after that (sheet rows, WhatsApp, email, follow-up) happens inside Pabbly and connected tools, not in this codebase.
secrets_in_use: RAZORPAY_KEY_ID and RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET (server side environment variables).
gaps_in_current_build: No database. Nothing is stored by the funnel itself; all records live in Pabbly or downstream tools.
No lead capture before payment. A visitor who never pays is not recorded at all.
No authentication, no users, no roles, no dashboard.
No first-party tracking. No UTM, fbclid or gclid capture is stored; no event stream.
No webhook from Razorpay to the server. If the customer closes the tab after paying, the success path may never run.
Customer details are carried in Razorpay order notes only.
No retry or monitoring on the Pabbly calls; failures are only logged to the console.
One landing page per deployment; no shared configuration across pages.

pain_points.title: Tool sprawl and recurring cost
pain_points.detail: Workflow, tracking and data tools are paid separately, per client, every month.

pain_points.title: Excel as the system of record
pain_points.detail: Sales works from spreadsheets that are copied, edited and shared with no control.

pain_points.title: No access control
pain_points.detail: A sheet is either shared or not. A salesperson cannot be limited to their own leads.

pain_points.title: No single view of performance
pain_points.detail: Revenue, leads and ad spend sit in different places, so campaign profitability is guesswork.

pain_points.title: Lost leads
pain_points.detail: Visitors who start but do not finish checkout are not stored anywhere.

pain_points.title: Fragile automation
pain_points.detail: If a Pabbly step fails nobody is alerted and the customer silently gets nothing.

pain_points.title: Vendor dependence
pain_points.detail: Workflows live in a vendor tool the client does not own.

pain_points.title: Slow launch of new pages
pain_points.detail: Every new landing page needs developer time to wire payments, tracking and automations again.

goals: Give every brand one central dashboard, with a dashboard per landing page.
Capture every lead, payment attempt and event in a database the client owns.
Enforce role-based visibility on the server, so a salesperson only ever sees their own leads.
Replace Pabbly with an in-house workflow engine.
Replace Trackify-style tracking with in-house first-party tracking.
Replace Excel with dashboards, filters and export on demand.
Integrate Razorpay and WhatsApp directly, with no automation middleman.
Make adding a new landing page a configuration task instead of a development task.
Give the Super Admin full control over what data goes where.
non_goals: Building our own payment gateway or moving money.
Becoming a WhatsApp provider; we integrate with the official Business API.
Replacing Meta Ads Manager or Google Ads.
A drag-and-drop landing page designer in phase 1.
A public marketplace or multi-tenant SaaS billing system in phase 1.
Native mobile apps in phase 1; the dashboard is responsive web.

hierarchy.name: Platform
hierarchy.description: The whole product. Owned and administered by the Super Admin.

hierarchy.name: Brand (client)
hierarchy.description: A business using the platform, for example FUME. A brand has its own users, branding, integrations and landing pages. Data of one brand is never visible to another brand.

hierarchy.name: Landing page
hierarchy.description: One funnel with its own URL, offer, payment configuration, workflow, tracking settings and content. A brand can have many landing pages.

hierarchy.name: Lead / customer
hierarchy.description: A person who interacted with a landing page. Holds contact details, source, events, payments, notes and status.

dashboards.name: Brand dashboard
shows: All landing pages of the brand as cards with key numbers
dashboards.opens_from: Login as Management, or Super Admin selecting a brand

dashboards.name: Landing page dashboard
shows: Leads and payments of that page
dashboards.opens_from: Clicking a landing page card on the brand dashboard

dashboards.name: Sales workspace
shows: Only the leads assigned to the logged-in salesperson
Follow-up tasks, notes, call and WhatsApp actions

platform_structure.navigation_rule: The same application serves everyone. The menu and the data change by role. There is no separate app for sales, developers or management.

principles: Every screen and every API call requires authentication. There are no anonymous dashboard endpoints.
Authorisation is enforced on the server for every request. Hiding a button in the interface is never the only protection.
Data is scoped by brand first, then by role. A user can only ever reach data of brands they belong to.
Sales users see only leads assigned to them. They cannot list, search or open any other lead, even by guessing a URL or an id.
The Super Admin defines roles, permissions, and where each kind of data is routed.
Every sensitive action (login, export, permission change, lead reassignment, configuration change) is written to an audit log.

roles.label: Super Admin
can: Create and suspend brands and landing pages
Create users and assign roles and brands
Define custom permissions and routing rules
Configure integrations (payments, WhatsApp, email, tracking) for any brand
See every lead, payment, event and report across all brands
Read the full audit log
Run exports and data deletion requests
Impersonate a role in read-only preview mode to verify what that role sees
cannot: Nothing is blocked, but every action is logged.

roles.label: Management
can: See all landing pages, leads, payments and reports of their brand(s)
See performance of every manager and salesperson
Edit landing page configuration and workflows if the Super Admin grants it
Export data of their brand(s)
Reassign leads between managers and salespeople

roles.label: Manager
roles.who: Team lead for a group of salespeople.
can: See leads assigned to themselves and to the salespeople in their team
Assign and reassign leads inside their team
See performance of their own team
Add notes, tasks and statuses
Export their team's leads if permitted
cannot: See revenue of the whole brand unless granted

roles.label: Sales
can: See only leads assigned to them
Update status, add notes, schedule follow-ups
Trigger allowed actions such as sending a WhatsApp template
See their own targets and performance
cannot: See any lead not assigned to them

roles.label: Developer
roles.who: Engineer connecting landing pages and maintaining workflows.
can: Create and rotate landing page keys and API credentials
Edit workflows and integration settings
See event logs, webhook deliveries, workflow run logs and error traces
Use a test mode with sandbox payments and test leads
cannot: See full customer personal data by default (masked unless the Super Admin grants it)
See payments of live customers in detail unless granted

permission_matrix.legend: Y = allowed, N = not allowed, Own = only own records, Team = own plus team records, Brand = whole brand, All = whole platform, Cfg = allowed if the Super Admin grants

rows.capability: Edit landing page content and offer

methods: Email and password with strong password rules
One-time code by email or WhatsApp as a second factor (recommended for Super Admin and Management)
sessions: Device and session list with remote revoke
Rate limiting and lockout on repeated failures
account_lifecycle: Invite by email, forced password set on first login
Deactivate instantly on exit; leads are reassigned
Role changes take effect on the next request

lead_visibility_rules: A lead belongs to exactly one brand and one landing page.
A lead has at most one current owner (a salesperson or unassigned).
Sales sees: leads where owner is the user.
Manager sees: leads where owner is the manager or any member of the manager's team.
Management sees: all leads of the brand.
Unassigned leads are visible to Manager and above and to a configurable shared queue for Sales if the Super Admin enables it.
Reassigning a lead immediately removes it from the previous owner's view.

modules.name: Landing page connector
modules.summary: The bridge between a landing page and the central platform. Defines how a page registers, authenticates, sends data and receives configuration.
modules.replaces: Per-page hard-coded wiring (Razorpay routes and Pabbly URLs copied into every funnel project).

connection_method.status: To be defined by the client. The connector is built behind one interface so the method can change without touching the rest of the platform.
default_proposal: Each landing page gets a public page key and a secret server key issued from its dashboard.
Browser side: a small first-party script sends tracking events and form submissions to the platform using the public key.
Server side: the landing page backend calls the platform API with the secret key for trusted actions such as creating an order or reading page configuration.
Configuration is fetched by the page at build or request time, so price, countdown, bonuses and copy can change from the dashboard without a redeploy.

features: Register a landing page: name, brand, domain(s), environment (test or live), status.
Issue, rotate and revoke page keys and secrets.
Allowed-origin list per page so only the page's own domains can send browser events.
Signed requests with timestamp and replay protection for server calls.
Page configuration endpoint returning offer, pricing, payment settings reference, tracking ids and content blocks.
Health check per page: last event received, last payment, error counts.
Test mode that routes to Razorpay test keys and marks data as test.
Versioned API so existing pages keep working when the platform evolves.
Starter kit: a ready Next.js module that drops into a funnel project and handles checkout, events and form submission.
acceptance: A new landing page can be registered and sending data within one working session of a developer.
Revoking a key stops that page's traffic immediately.
A request with a bad signature or from a disallowed origin is rejected and logged.

modules.name: Leads and CRM
modules.summary: A single database of every person who touched a landing page, replacing Excel as the working tool for sales.
modules.replaces: Excel and Google Sheet lead files.
features: Lead record: name, email, phone (normalised), brand, landing page, source, UTM, campaign, ad, device, location (city level), first seen, last seen.
Lead creation at the earliest moment: form submit or checkout start, not only after payment.
De-duplication by phone and email with merge history.
Status pipeline: New, Contacted, Interested, Paid, Refunded, Not interested, Lost. Statuses are configurable per brand.
Tags and custom fields per brand.
Notes and activity timeline: events, payments, messages, calls, status changes.
Assignment: manual, round robin, or rule based (for example by landing page or city).
Follow-up tasks with due dates and reminders.
Saved views and filters: by page, source, status, owner, date, payment state.
Bulk actions: assign, tag, change status, send a template (permission permitting).
Strict visibility by role as defined in roles_and_access.
Search by name, phone or email, limited to what the role may see.
acceptance: A salesperson who searches for a lead assigned to someone else gets no result, and a direct URL to it returns not found.
A visitor who starts checkout and never pays appears as a lead with state 'checkout started'.
Every status or owner change appears in the lead's timeline with who and when.

modules.name: Payments with Razorpay
modules.summary: Direct Razorpay integration with orders, signature verification, webhooks, failures and refunds, written to the platform database.
modules.replaces: The Pabbly success and failure webhooks as the only record of payments.
features: Per landing page Razorpay configuration (key id and encrypted secret), with test and live modes.
Server-created orders with the amount taken from the page configuration, never from the browser.
Signature verification on the success callback.
Razorpay webhook endpoint for payment.captured, payment.failed, order.paid and refund events, so payment is recorded even if the customer closes the tab.
Idempotent processing: the same event delivered twice creates one payment record.
Payment states: created, attempted, captured, failed, refunded, partially refunded.
Failure reasons captured from Razorpay and shown to sales for follow-up.
Refund from the dashboard (permission controlled) calling the Razorpay refund API.
Reconciliation view: platform records versus Razorpay, with mismatches flagged.
Invoice or receipt generation per payment, with brand details and GST fields where applicable.
No card data ever touches the platform; only Razorpay ids and statuses are stored.
acceptance: A captured payment appears on the lead and on the landing page dashboard within seconds, without any third-party tool.
Closing the browser right after paying still results in a recorded payment through the webhook.
Duplicate webhook delivery does not double count revenue.

modules.name: Workflow engine
modules.summary: An in-house automation engine that runs the sequences currently built inside Pabbly.
features: Triggers: lead created, form submitted, checkout started, checkout abandoned after N minutes, payment captured, payment failed, refund issued, status changed, tag added, scheduled time.

Actions: send WhatsApp template, send email, send SMS (if a provider is configured), assign lead, create follow-up task, change status, add tag, call an external webhook, wait, branch on a condition, stop.
Conditions: by landing page, source, amount, city, tag, status, time of day.
Visual or form-based editor with a readable summary of each workflow.
Per landing page workflows plus brand-wide default workflows that pages can inherit.
Test mode: run a workflow against a test lead and see each step.
Run history for every execution: input, each step result, timing, error.
Automatic retries with backoff; permanent failures raise an alert to the Developer and Super Admin.
Rate limits and quiet hours so messages are not sent at night.
Versioning: edits create a new version; running executions finish on the version they started with.
Import of the existing Pabbly flow structure as a starting template, rebuilt by us, not executed through Pabbly.

example_workflows.name: Payment success
steps: Trigger: payment captured
Mark lead as Paid
Send WhatsApp confirmation template
Send email receipt
Assign to a salesperson by round robin
Create task: call within 2 hours

example_workflows.name: Payment failed
steps: Trigger: payment failed
Wait 10 minutes
Send WhatsApp message with a retry link
If still unpaid after 24 hours, assign for a call

example_workflows.name: Abandoned checkout
steps: Trigger: checkout started and no payment after 15 minutes
Send WhatsApp reminder
Wait 1 day
Send final reminder
Tag as abandoned

acceptance: A workflow failure is visible in run history and triggers an alert; nothing fails silently.
Editing a workflow does not interrupt executions already in progress.

modules.name: WhatsApp integration
modules.summary: Direct integration with the official WhatsApp Business API for template messages, replies and delivery status.
modules.replaces: WhatsApp steps inside Pabbly and manual WhatsApp from personal phones.
modules.keeps: The WhatsApp Business API provider (Meta Cloud API or an approved business solution provider).
features: Connect a WhatsApp Business number per brand.
Template management: create, submit for approval, track approval status.
Send templates from workflows and manually from a lead.
Inbound messages shown on the lead timeline when the customer replies.
Delivery, read and failure status per message.
Opt-in tracking: store when and how the customer agreed to be messaged.
Opt-out handling: stop messaging on request.
Message cost visibility per brand so conversation charges are not a surprise.
Per role permission: sales can send only approved templates to their own leads.
acceptance: A paid customer receives the confirmation template automatically, and the delivery status appears on the lead.
A customer who opts out is never messaged again by any workflow.
modules.external_dependency: Meta business verification and template approval take time and are outside our control.

modules.name: Email and SMS notifications
modules.summary: Transactional and follow-up email and optional SMS from the platform.
modules.replaces: Email and SMS steps inside Pabbly.
modules.keeps: An email delivery provider and, if used, an SMS provider (these cannot be self-hosted reliably).
features: Email templates with brand logo and colours.
Receipt and confirmation emails after payment.
Internal alerts to staff: new paid lead, failed workflow, daily summary.
Delivery and bounce tracking.
Unsubscribe handling for non-transactional mail.
SMS for OTP and urgent reminders where a provider is configured.

modules.name: First-party tracking
modules.summary: An in-house tracking system, similar in purpose to Trackify, that records visitor behaviour and attributes revenue to its source.
features: A lightweight script served from the client's own domain, sending events to the platform.
Events: page view, scroll depth, video play, video progress milestones, CTA click, form start, form submit, checkout start, payment attempt, payment success, payment failure.
Visitor and session identifiers using first-party storage, respecting consent settings.
Capture of UTM parameters, fbclid, gclid, referrer, landing URL, device type, browser, approximate city.
First-touch and last-touch attribution stored on the lead and on each payment.
Server-side events for payments, so revenue is tracked even if the browser closes.
Forwarding of conversions to Meta Conversions API and Google Ads or GA4, configured from the dashboard, with event de-duplication.
Event debugger: see live events from a page while testing.
Per landing page instructions for connecting Meta Ads and Google Ads, shown inside the dashboard.
Bot and duplicate traffic filtering.
Data retention settings.
acceptance: For any payment, the dashboard shows the campaign and ad that first brought the visitor and the one that last touched them.
A conversion sent to Meta is also stored locally, and a mismatch is flagged.
modules.external_dependency: Meta and Google must still receive conversion events for ad optimisation. That is outbound data to them, not a replacement of them.

modules.name: Analytics and reporting
modules.summary: Dashboards for management and managers covering funnel, revenue, sources and team performance.
features: Per landing page: visitors, leads, checkout starts, payments, revenue, conversion rate at each step.
Funnel drop-off with step-by-step percentages.
Video engagement: plays and watch milestones for VSL pages.
Source breakdown: by UTM source, campaign and ad, including revenue and cost per acquisition when ad cost is entered or imported.
Return on ad spend where spend is available.
Team performance: leads handled, contact rate, conversion, revenue by salesperson and manager.
Date range, comparison with previous period, and filters by brand and page.
Scheduled summary emails (daily or weekly) per role.
Role-aware numbers: a salesperson sees only their own numbers.

modules.name: Landing page content and configuration
modules.summary: Edit offer and page content from the dashboard instead of changing code.
modules.replaces: Editing constants in the funnel codebase (price, countdown, bonuses, testimonials).
features: Offer settings: price, original price, countdown length, CTA labels, refund text.
Content blocks: headline, subheadline, bonuses, benefits, testimonials, FAQs, founder story.
Media library: images and video links reused across pages.
Draft and publish with preview.
Version history and rollback.
Clone a landing page configuration to start a new one.
Simple A/B test: split traffic between two versions of a page and compare conversion.
modules.note: Page layouts are still built as code in phase 1. The dashboard controls the content and offer that the layout renders.

modules.name: Exports and data portability
modules.summary: Excel and CSV export on demand, replacing the habit of living inside spreadsheets.
features: Export leads, payments, events and reports to CSV or Excel.
Exports respect role scope: a user can only export what they can see.
Column selection and saved export templates.
Large exports run in the background and arrive as a download link.
Every export is audit logged with user, filter and row count.
Optional watermarking or masking of phone numbers for lower roles.

modules.name: Super Admin console
modules.summary: Central control: brands, pages, users, roles, routing and system health.
modules.replaces: Ad hoc setup spread across many tools.
features: Create and suspend brands and landing pages.
Invite users and assign role and brand.
Routing rules: which data from which page goes to which team, workflow or integration.
Integration vault: encrypted storage of Razorpay, WhatsApp, email and tracking credentials.
System health: queue depth, failed jobs, webhook delivery status, error rates.
Feature flags per brand to switch modules on or off.
Data retention and deletion requests.
Read-only role preview to verify what a role sees.

modules.name: Audit log and security
modules.summary: A tamper-evident record of who did what, plus the security controls around it.
features: Log of logins, failed logins, permission changes, configuration edits, exports, refunds, lead reassignments.
Filter by user, action, brand and time.
Encrypted secrets, hashed passwords, TLS everywhere.
Per-IP and per-account rate limits.
Optional IP allow list for Super Admin.
Backups with tested restore.
Data masking for roles that do not need full contact details.

modules.name: Branding and white label
modules.summary: Each brand sees its own logo and colours in the dashboard and in messages.
features: Logo, colours and name per brand.
Custom domain for the dashboard per brand.
Brand-specific email and WhatsApp sender details.
Receipts and invoices with the brand's identity.

modules.name: Developer tools
modules.summary: Everything a developer needs to connect and debug a landing page.
features: Key and secret management per page.
Live event stream and webhook delivery log.
Workflow run traces.
Test mode and sample data generator.
API documentation with examples.
Sandbox that mimics Razorpay events for end-to-end testing.
Starter kit and a checklist for connecting a new page.

what_we_replace.used_for_today: Success and failure automations triggered by webhooks: sheet rows, WhatsApp, email, follow-up.
what_we_replace.replaced_by: Module M4 Workflow engine, with direct WhatsApp (M5) and email (M6).
what_changes_for_the_client: Automations are visible, versioned and logged inside the platform.
Failures raise alerts instead of failing silently.
what_we_replace.migration: Existing flows are documented and rebuilt as native workflows, then run in parallel for a short period before Pabbly is switched off.

what_we_replace.replaced_by: Module M7 First-party tracking and M8 Analytics.
what_changes_for_the_client: Tracking script served from the client's own domain.
Revenue attributed to campaign and ad inside the same dashboard as leads.
what_we_replace.migration: Run the new tracking alongside the old one, compare numbers, then retire the old tool.

what_we_replace.tool: Excel and Google Sheets for leads and payments
what_we_replace.used_for_today: System of record for leads, payments and sales follow-up.
what_we_replace.replaced_by: Module M2 Leads and CRM, M3 Payments, M10 Exports.
what_changes_for_the_client: Sales works inside the platform, not in shared files.
Each salesperson sees only their own leads.
Excel export remains available on demand, but it is no longer the source of truth.
what_we_replace.migration: Import existing sheets once as historical leads; stop writing to sheets after cut-over.

what_we_replace.tool: Separate dashboards per client or per team
what_we_replace.used_for_today: Different views for sales, developers and management in different tools.
what_changes_for_the_client: Roles decide what each person sees.
what_we_replace.migration: Create users and roles, assign leads, then switch teams over.

what_we_replace.used_for_today: Price, countdown, bonuses and copy edited in code.
what_we_replace.replaced_by: Module M9 Content and configuration, M1 Connector.
what_changes_for_the_client: Offer changes without a developer or a redeploy.
New landing pages start from a copied configuration.
what_we_replace.migration: Move current constants into page configuration once the connector is live.

what_we_do_not_replace.why: Moving money requires a licensed payment gateway. We integrate with it directly and remove the middle tool between it and the client.
Messages must travel through Meta's official network, directly or through an approved provider.
what_we_do_not_replace.cost_that_remains: Per-conversation charges from Meta or the provider, and any provider fee.

what_we_do_not_replace.why: These are where ads run. We send them conversion events and show their results next to ours.
Reliable inbox delivery needs an established sending infrastructure.
The platform needs servers. They belong to the client, not to a tool vendor.
Streaming video at scale is best left to a video host or CDN.
Page layouts and creative are still designed and built as code. The platform manages their content, offer and data.
what_we_do_not_replace.cost_that_remains: Design and build effort per page.

honest_note_on_third_party_dependence: 'No third party' is true for the tools that sit between the pieces: workflow automation, tracking and spreadsheets.
It is not true for the services that do things only a regulated or global network can do: payments, WhatsApp, ads, email and SMS delivery.
The saving is the recurring subscription of the middle tools, plus the control and ownership of the data. It is not the removal of all running costs.

landing_page_connection.status: Method to be confirmed by the client. Steps below follow the default proposal.
steps: Developer or Super Admin creates the landing page in the dashboard and picks the brand.
The platform issues a page key and secret.
The page installs the starter kit and sets the keys in its environment.
The page loads its configuration from the platform.
The page sends events and form submissions; the Developer checks the live event view.
Razorpay keys for that page are stored in the integration vault.
A test payment in test mode is run end to end.
The page is switched to live and starts counting.

visitor_to_lead: Visitor lands on a page from an ad; the script records UTM, click ids and referrer.
Page view and engagement events are sent.
Visitor starts checkout and enters name, email and phone.
At that moment the platform creates or updates the lead with state 'checkout started' and stores the attribution.
If the visitor leaves, the abandoned checkout workflow can follow up.
payment_success: Server creates a Razorpay order using the amount from page configuration.
Browser sends the result to the server and Razorpay also calls the platform webhook.
The platform verifies the signature, records the payment once (idempotent), marks the lead Paid.
Server-side conversion is forwarded to Meta and Google.
The payment-success workflow runs: confirmation message, receipt email, assignment to a salesperson, follow-up task.
The lead appears on the landing page dashboard and on the assigned salesperson's workspace.
Managers and management see the updated numbers immediately.
payment_failure: Razorpay reports failure through the browser and the webhook.
The platform records the attempt with the failure reason.
The payment-failed workflow sends a retry message and, if needed, assigns a call.
Sales sees the reason on the lead.
sales_followup: Salesperson opens their workspace and sees only their assigned leads.
They open a lead, read the timeline, call or message, and update the status.
Notes and tasks are saved on the timeline.
Manager reviews team performance; management reviews the brand.
export: User chooses a filter and columns.
The platform checks role scope and builds the file in the background.
A download link is delivered; the export is audit logged.
new_user_onboarding: Super Admin or Management invites a user by email with a role and brand.
The user sets a password and, if required, a second factor.
The user lands on the view for their role.

Browser sends tracking events with the public key.
Create or update a lead from a form or checkout start.

architecture.principle: Boring, proven components. Own the code, the data and the infrastructure.

proposed_stack.dashboard_frontend: Next.js with TypeScript, responsive web, role-aware navigation.
proposed_stack.backend_api: A single API service (Node.js with TypeScript or the team's preferred stack) with clear modules per area.
proposed_stack.queue_and_scheduler: A job queue (for example Redis based) for workflows, retries, exports and scheduled tasks.
proposed_stack.cache: Redis for sessions, rate limits and short-lived data.
proposed_stack.file_storage: Object storage for exports and media.
proposed_stack.events_store: High-volume tracking events in partitioned PostgreSQL tables first; move to a columnar store only if volume demands it.
proposed_stack.observability: Structured logs, error tracking and uptime alerts.

architecture.note_on_stack: The stack is a recommendation. The platform is designed so that the choice can follow the client's team skills.
deployment: Separate worker process for the queue
security: Passwords hashed with a modern algorithm
Secrets encrypted at rest and never returned by the API
Row-level scoping enforced in the data layer by brand and owner
Rate limiting and brute force protection
Regular backups and a tested restore
Least-privilege access for staff and for the application itself
scalability: Event ingestion accepts quickly and processes asynchronously.
Dashboards read from pre-aggregated tables for common reports.
Landing pages never block on the platform: if the platform is unreachable, checkout still works and events are queued and replayed.
reliability: Payment recorded through both browser callback and Razorpay webhook.
Workflow steps retry with backoff, with alerts on permanent failure.
Health page for the Super Admin.

compliance_and_privacy: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act applies to personal data of customers. The platform supports consent records, purpose limits, access and deletion requests.
WhatsApp messaging requires opt-in. Opt-in and opt-out are stored and respected by every workflow.
Card details are never stored. Razorpay handles card data.
Health-related context in leads (for a wellness brand) is treated as sensitive: masked for roles that do not need it, never used in message text beyond what the customer expects.
Retention periods are configurable per brand; exports and deletions are logged.
GST invoice fields are supported on receipts where required.
Legal pages (privacy policy, disclaimer, terms) remain the client's responsibility to author and approve.

faq.q: Will we really not pay anyone monthly?
faq.a: You stop paying the workflow and tracking tools. You still pay the providers that do the real work: Razorpay fees, WhatsApp conversation charges, email or SMS usage, hosting and ad spend.

faq.q: Can a salesperson see all leads?
faq.a: No. A salesperson sees only the leads assigned to them. This is enforced on the server.
Yes, as an export. Data lives in the platform; Excel is a copy you download when needed.

faq.q: What happens to our current Pabbly flows?
faq.a: They are documented and rebuilt as native workflows, run in parallel for a short time, and then Pabbly is switched off.

faq.q: What if the platform goes down?
faq.a: Landing pages keep working. Events are queued and replayed, and payments are also confirmed through Razorpay webhooks.

faq.q: Can we add a new landing page ourselves?
faq.a: Once the connector is in place, a developer registers the page and connects it in a short session. Content and offer are then edited from the dashboard.
The client. It lives in the client's own database and hosting account.

faq.q: Do you build the landing page designs too?
faq.a: Layouts are built as code per page and are quoted separately from the platform.
